title: Prevent Siphonage: Understanding Proper P-Trap Venting
description: Drain traps rely on a continuous standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. A critical hazard occurs when an unvented trap or S-trap configuration causes self-siphonage. When water drains rapidly through an unvented trap arm, it creates a negative pressure vacuum that pulls the liquid seal out of the P-trap as flow stops. To maintain a reliable water seal, ensure the trap arm distance and vent placement comply with local plumbing code standards, preventing vacuum creation.

Prevent Siphonage: Understanding Proper P-Trap Venting

Drain traps rely on a continuous standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. A critical hazard occurs when an unvented trap or S-trap configuration causes self-siphonage. When water drains rapidly through an unvented trap arm, it creates a negative pressure vacuum that pulls the liquid seal out of the P-trap as flow stops. To maintain a reliable water seal, ensure the trap arm distance and vent placement comply with local plumbing code standards, preventing vacuum creation.
